alignments.note: Rule 77: a relative pronoun expanded with the generic noun things heads on things.
Participle ἔχοντα → have, the ASV writing one verb word for the periphrasis's lexical element.
Rule 70: the ASV writes indeed for μέν, so it is its own aligned unit on that word.
λόγον → a show, with the supplied indefinite determiner as a rule 51 helper on the anarthrous noun.
Determinerless genitive: of rides with the noun under rule 21.
ἐν → in.
ἐθελοθρησκία → will worship; rule 66 heads on the noun, which glosses the θρησκεία element, while will renders the ἐθελο- prefix.
Coordinating καί.
ταπεινοφροσύνῃ → humility.
Coordinating καί.
ἀφειδίᾳ → severity.
Anarthrous genitive: no article stands, so the English preposition realizing the relation and the supplied determiner are rule 21/51 helpers on the noun.

Rule 86: the ASV supplies an adversative but where no Greek conjunction stands. μέν is already spent on indeed under rule 70, and rule 70 forbids joining the correlation to a word elsewhere, so no source token licenses this.

The finite ἐστιν governs both predicates; the ASV writes have for the participial predicate and supplies are for the second, so the finite copula is realized there. Marking are added and leaving ἐστιν unrepresented remains defensible.
Ordinary negative → not; the following indefinite is not a negative, so rules 41 and 59 do not empty it.
ἐν → of.
Indefinite τινι → any.
τιμῇ → value (margin: honor).
πρός → against.
Anarthrous πλησμονήν: no article competes, so the supplied determiner is a rule 51 helper on the noun.
Rule 21: of the on the article, headed on the.
σαρκός → flesh.

review_notes: The verse's one genuinely open choice is where the finite ἐστιν lands: I give it the supplied are of the second predicate, since ἔχοντα already has have and the ASV's are continues the same finite verb over the second predicate. The alternative is to leave ἐστιν unrepresented and mark are added.
The supplied but is added under rule 86: μέν has its own word (indeed) under rule 70 and no δέ or other conjunction stands in the verse.
